summary: One finding: training.py line 93 references `nn.CrossEntropyLoss()` but `nn` (torch.nn) is not imported, causing a NameError at runtime. All field-guide checks otherwise pass — essential features are properly implemented and annotated, the architecture substitution is documented, and the training protocol matches the spec.

findings.description: Line 93 uses `nn.CrossEntropyLoss()` but `nn` (torch.nn) is not imported. The imports (lines 13-19) include `torch`, `torch.optim as optim`, `TensorDataset`, `DataLoader`, and `MCDropoutMLP`, but not `torch.nn`. This causes a NameError at runtime, breaking the entire training function. The fix is to add `import torch.nn as nn` (or use `torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss()`).
findings.proposed_fix: Add `import torch.nn as nn` to the imports in method/training.py.

checks_summary.note: model.py has nn.Dropout(p=dropout_rate) at lines 60, 66 (dropout active at inference). forward() returns raw logits from the final Linear layer (line 69, no softmax). # essential annotations at lines 31-32 match the actual code.

Module docstring (lines 7-19) explicitly documents the CNN→MLP substitution, preserves the essential contract (dropout at inference, logits output, recommended dropout rate 0.5), and names the silent-failure mode for the bayesian AL paradigm.
training.py uses `nn.CrossEntropyLoss()` without importing `torch.nn as nn` (NameError at runtime). The optimizer (Adam), protocol (retrain from scratch), and seeding are otherwise correct per spec.

Architecture has nn.Dropout layers (lines 60, 66). Nothing in model.py disables them. The bayesian-specific check confirms the architecture supports MC dropout scoring (which method.py will handle by calling model.train() before inference).
